title: Energy Storage Systems
painPoint: Battery energy storage systems rely on high-current DC contactors, magnetic latching relays, and Hall-effect current sensors that must operate flawlessly under sustained thermal loads exceeding 150 degrees Celsius near power semiconductors. Standard NdFeB grades suffer irreversible flux loss at these temperatures, causing contactor chatter, relay dropout, and eventual weld failure. Transient short-circuit currents generate powerful opposing fields that can partially demagnetize low-coercivity magnets, degrading actuation force across millions of switching cycles. Engineers struggle to source magnets delivering both high energy product for compact contactor design and reliable high-temperature stability, while maintaining tight coercivity tolerances for consistent trip thresholds in safety-critical battery disconnect circuits.
youjiuSolution: YOUJIU supplies high-coercivity NdFeB magnets engineered for energy storage DC contactors and magnetic relays, offering grades such as 42SH for 150-degree service, 38UH and 33EH for 180-degree continuous operation. Our magnets feature elevated Hcj values above 20 kOe to withstand fault-current demagnetization, ensuring stable actuation force over ten million cycles. Nickel and epoxy coatings provide corrosion resistance in humid battery enclosures. Every production lot is characterized by full hysteresis-loop testing and flux-density mapping. Share your contactor force-stroke curve and thermal profile with YOUJIU to receive a grade recommendation, pricing, and technical datasheet optimized for your storage system.
advantages: High-coercivity grades 42SH, 38UH, and 33EH for 150 to 180 degree Celsius continuous service.
Hcj values exceeding 20 kOe resist demagnetization from transient fault-current pulses.
Full hysteresis-loop testing and flux mapping guarantee batch-to-batch actuation-force consistency.
